findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Jira Cloud indexes Jira issue JSON under `jira:cloud:issues`; it does not provide `start_epoch`, `end_epoch`, `issue_type` or `service_ci`. The text does not name the JSM change fields holding the planned window (the change start / completion date custom fields), how they are converted, or how the affected service is derived, so the SPL returns nothing out of the box.
findings.quote: Require ISO timestamps in custom fields; normalize to epoch at ingest.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the source fields (look up the customfield IDs for the JSM 'Change start date' / 'Change completion date' fields and the affected-service field in your instance), give the props.conf EVAL/FIELDALIAS or search-time `eval strptime(...)` that produces `start_epoch` / `end_epoch`, alias `fields.issuetype.name` to `issue_type`, and explain how `service_ci` is populated.

findings.explanation: The SPL never calls a lookup; it expects `service_ci` already on the event, so the 'CMDB lookup' is undocumented and unused. The Jira Cloud add-on is an API-polling modular input configured from its Inputs tab in Splunk Web (heavy forwarder or search tier), not something run on a Universal Forwarder.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Jira Cloud (6211) + CMDB lookup `service_ci` — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
findings.suggested_fix: List Splunk Add-on for Jira Cloud (6211) on a heavy forwarder / Splunk Cloud IDM; if a CMDB mapping is needed, name the lookup and add the `lookup ... OUTPUT service_ci` step to the documented search, otherwise drop the lookup reference.

findings.explanation: The SPL also reads `sourcetype=jira:issue`, which the Jira Cloud add-on does not produce (its sourcetypes are `jira:cloud:issues`, `jira:cloud:audit:log`, `jira:cloud:users`); the sourcetypes and index are not named here.
findings.quote: Jira Service Management change tickets with planned start/end
findings.suggested_fix: State `index=itsm sourcetype=jira:cloud:issues` from add-on 6211 and, if Jira Data Center is in scope, name the separate input that produces `jira:issue`.

findings.explanation: Overlap detection needs every approved change whose window is still in the future, but `_time` on Jira issue events reflects ingestion/update, so a 24-hour window only sees changes touched in the last day and misses collisions with older approvals. The duplicated generic Steps 1–5 also add a 'vendor admin UI inventory count' check and severity routing that do not apply.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Search back far enough to cover all open changes (or maintain a KV-store of the latest state per change key), keep the latest event per `key` (`dedup key`), and filter to `end_epoch > now()`; remove the duplicated template steps.

findings.explanation: The search does not check approval status (it keeps any issue of type Change or label `change`), so 'approved' describes the intent in the title, not what the detection does.
findings.quote: We look for two approved change windows on top of each other
findings.suggested_fix: Either say 'two planned change windows for the same service' or note that the search must be limited to CAB-approved changes.

findings.explanation: Splunk has no built-in Gantt visualization, and an alert email is an alert action rather than a visualization; the reader is not told how to build the view.
findings.quote: Gantt-style table, Alert email to CAB.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe a table sorted by `service_ci` and `start` showing both change keys and their windows (or name the Splunkbase Gantt/timeline visualization if one is intended), and move the CAB email to the alert-action step.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `streamstats window=1 current=f latest(end)` compares each change only with the immediately preceding change per service; a long change that spans several later ones is missed for all but the first. Use the running `max(end)` of all previous changes per `service_ci`. Re-ingested updates of the same issue are also not deduplicated before sorting.
No status filter for CAB approval although the title says 'CAB-Approved Windows'; cancelled, rejected or draft changes produce collisions.

summary: The goal (flag overlapping change windows on the same service) is clear, but the sidecar never explains how `start_epoch`, `end_epoch`, `issue_type` and `service_ci` come to exist on raw Jira Cloud issue events, promises a CMDB lookup the SPL never performs, mis-describes where the add-on runs, and its scheduling advice would miss most approved future changes.
